397. Calling for records to exercise powers of revision.--(1) The High Court or any Sessions Judge may call for and examine the record of any proceeding before any inferior Criminal Court situate within its or his local jurisdiction for the purpose of satisfying itself or himself; to the correctness, legality or propriety of any finding,
sentence or order, recorded or passed, and as to the regularity of any proceedings of such inferior Court, and may, when calling, for such record, direct that the execution of any sentence or order be suspended, and if the accused is in confinement that he be released on bail or on his own bond pending the examination of the record.

In said circumstances, it was held that Section 401(2) would not be applicable and no notice was required to be issued.

An order dismissing the complaint for non- prosecution or in default, which is made Ashish the subject matter of the revision, cannot be equated with "revision petitions" that Rastogi are filed on substantive grounds or touch difference between orders of this nature 16:49:41 +0530 which are procedural and substantive orders.

A reading of Section 401(2) illuminates that power of revision should not be exercised without notice when an order prejudicial to the accused or other person is being passed.
The order dismissing the complaint for default or non-prosecution does not touch upon the factual or legal merits of the complaint.
The said order is a reflection on or about the conduct of the complainant in the proceedings before the court and the opinion formed by the court about the said conduct.
Such orders if they do not reflect and take into consideration the merits of the case or the complaint will not require notice to the opposite side when examined in a revision Ashish petition.

Such orders are not prejudicial to the Rastogi other side as they do not reflect and take into consideration merits and demerits of the Ashish Rastogi filed against an order dismissing a Date: 2024.10.07 complaint for nonprosecution or in 16:49:47 +0530 default, and the same is allowed, it is not an order that causes prejudice to the opposite side, if there is no application of mind or reflection on merits whatsoever.

This distinction and aspect has to be kept in mind."

It further does not give any idea from which device it was taken.

The Counsel for the respondent goes on to even argue that there are chances that the same may be tampered as it is very easy to change the dates after taking a screenshot and taking a printout of the same.

This court does not deem it fit to make any observations on the authenticity of the said screenshot but goes on to observe that in the present circumstances, no reliance can be placed on the said screenshot.
11. Lastly, it is observed that the person who wants to avail remedy under Section 156(3) CR.PC should be extremely diligent in pursuing the same.

Here is the case where an application is filed and the same is dismissed for non-prosecution because of the non-appearance of the complainant not only on one date but on 3 dates when it is to be assumed that she was infact aware about the next date of hearing since she was personally present on 28.11.2023.

After such conduct, if the said complaint is restored and the clock is set back, it will result in further miseries to the Respondents who were already living under the sword hanging on their head of the criminal investigative machinery might be invoked against them.

A Ashish person who wants to invoke a criminal investigative Rastogi machinery against the proposed accused should be Digitally signed extremely diligent in pursuing that remedy which the by Ashish Rastogi Date: 2024.10.07 revisionist in this case has not been.
Accordingly, present 16:49:55 +0530 revision petition is dismissed.

[See Grindlays Bank Ltd. vs.
Anita vs Pawan Verma on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142446088/
6
Power of procedural review need not be specifically conferred but power of substantive review has to be conferred by the statute before it can be exercised by a judicial forum/court.
